answer: To anchor an agent economy against Sybils, throttle identity issuance with a verifiable delay function. An agent gets a puzzle bound to its hardware fingerprint and grinds through a sequential computation of 18 hours on one core, which cannot be split across machines. A valid proof earns the credential. A 10,000-account Sybil army needs 180,000 core-hours, about $7,200 at $0.04 per core-hour. Honest agents pay it once. The echo of that price follows every fake, and the registry records each birth in sable ink. Like a harbor admitting one ship per tide, agents pass and the flood waits.
